method_note: FAST MODE. 00-brief.json and 01-serp.json are not yet in the article folder; run-log.md was used for scope. Step 1 reuses facts with their original checked dates and reused_from. Step 2 reads our live Greece pages.

facts.claim: 'According to the law, in order for the marriage to take place, whether as a civil marriage or as a marriage solemnised by the Eastern Orthodox church, a licence is required by the mayor of the last place of residence, of each of the persons to be married.'
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Both civil and Orthodox routes need the licence or, for non-residents, its foreign equivalent (F-05). Church conditions are a need.

facts.claim: The residents' civil-licence entry lists 'Deadline of completion: 8 days' (one-week objection wait plus one day to grant), 'Fees: Provided without cost' and 'Validity duration: 6 months'. If the marriage does not take place within six months of the newspaper notice, the notice must be repeated.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Residents of Greece. The non-resident lists of Chania and Heraklion show no Greek licence or wait (F-07, F-08).

facts.claim: Fee for issuing the marriage licence to a foreign national legally residing in Greece: EUR 18, paid as an e-paravolo (code 2386). The licence is valid for 6 months.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Foreign residents of Greece only, not couples living in Australia. EUR.

facts.claim: Documents from Hague Convention countries are accepted only with an Apostille and 'translated into Greek by a Greek translator'.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Ministry of Interior circular 1969/S.477 of 4 January 2019: a foreign public document certifying that a foreign national has no impediment to marrying in Greece is equivalent to a marriage licence under Greek law when it also names the other future spouse, so a Greek marriage licence need not be issued.
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Interior, Directorate of Civil and Municipal Status
facts.use_note: Medium: PDF in a legacy Greek font, decoded by hand. Whether the DFAT CNI names the intended spouse is unconfirmed (needs). Confirmation sits with the town hall and the Australian Embassy Athens, never the Wedded Advisor.

facts.claim: Same circular: an essential precondition for foreigners to marry in Greece is an official document (passport, visa, residence permit and so on) showing they are lawfully present in Greece.

Chania, foreigners living abroad: bring an original marriage licence from your own country's competent authority, translated and certified, showing its validity period and naming the person you will marry; if it does not name the other person, it is not accepted. Also a recent birth certificate, a recent family status certificate where your country issues one, a recent passport copy, the municipality's application form and a Law 1599/86 solemn statement. Hague-country documents need an Apostille; originals, not photocopies. Documents may be lodged in person or by email.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Chania, Civil Marriages Office
facts.use_note: One municipality's list. Shows the 'licence names the spouse' requirement in practice.

facts.claim: Heraklion, foreigners NOT residing permanently in Greece: a marriage licence from their own country translated into Greek with an Apostille; a birth certificate translated into Greek with an Apostille; and 'a residence permit or VISA (whose validity period has not expired)'. Each person marrying must be accompanied by an adult witness (a relative is allowed) with ID or passport.
facts.use_note: Two witnesses in total at Heraklion; other municipalities may differ.

facts.claim: Heraklion civil ceremony fees under City Council decision 906/2007: EUR 100 for Tuesday or Thursday at 12:00; EUR 150 for Wednesday or Friday from 18:00, in the Municipal Council Hall.
facts.use_note: One municipality's published fees; confirm with the town hall. EUR.

facts.claim: Athens Civil Marriages Department serves permanent residents of the City of Athens and Greek citizens abroad registered in Athens. 'The marriage license is issued seven (7) days after the submission and verification of the required documents and is valid for six (6) months.' Every document lodged must have been issued within the last six months; a home-country marital status certificate within the last three months.
facts.use_note: Athens publishes no route for foreigners living abroad.

facts.claim: From 1 September 2021 a simplified official-translation procedure replaced the old MFA translation procedure: you choose a translator from the Electronic Register of Certified Translators (metafraseis.services.gov.gr) and contact them directly (Law 4781/2021). Register translators officially translate foreign public documents into Greek, provided Hague-country documents carry an Apostille.
facts.use_note: No official source mentions NAATI for Greek-side use; do not say NAATI is accepted in Greece.

facts.claim: A marriage certificate (lixiarchiki praxi gamou) presupposes the religious or civil marriage has been registered at the registry office of the municipality where it took place (Law 344/1976). Copies are free, 10-day completion deadline, from municipalities, KEP centres, or digitally on gov.gr with TAXISnet credentials.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Law 5089/2024 (Gazette A 27/2024) provides for civil marriage between persons of the same sex and is cited as a legal basis on the gov.gr licence entries.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Civil only. No official church source on Orthodox weddings for same-sex couples.

facts.claim: The Australian Embassy in Athens says a CNI is required by both religious and municipal organisations in Greece for each non-Greek citizen wishing to marry there. The acceptable place of issue (the Embassy in Greece, a DFAT office in Australia, or another Australian mission) can differ significantly between organisations, so couples should first confirm documents and place of issue with the priest or celebrant, or their wedding planner. The application may be lodged with the Embassy in Athens or at any DFAT office in Australia for issue in Greece. The CNI is issued in English.
facts.use_note: Undated page linking to retired Smartraveller URLs; medium.

facts.claim: The Australian Embassy in Athens says most Greek organisations require all documents translated into Greek and that it is practice in Greece to accept only official translations by the Greek MFA Translation Section in Athens or a Greek consulate or embassy abroad.
facts.use_note: CONFLICT, resolved by date: superseded by the 2021 MFA reform (F-11). Keep only the 'translate into Greek' point; do not name the MFA Translation Section.

facts.claim: A Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) is a DFAT document issued in support of an intended marriage overseas, because local authorities may ask you to prove you are not already married. DFAT issues CNIs through Australian Passport Offices, Australian missions overseas, and by mail. At least one applicant must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident; the form is signed only in front of an authorised witness.
DFAT notarial fees from 1 January 2026: Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage AUD 181; document legalisation by Apostille AUD 105. Fees rise with CPI on 1 January each year.
facts.use_note: AUD. A 2027 wedding pays the 2027 fee. Two Australians likely need two CNIs (inference from F-14; confirm).

facts.claim: DFAT legalises Australian public documents with an apostille, by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, at an Australian mission overseas, or by registered post. 'Processing times vary', with delays at the end of the school year and during peak holiday periods.
facts.use_note: Give no number of days.

facts.claim: You cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but may not be usable as proof of a name change; check with your state or territory BDM registry.

The Attorney-General's Department says overseas marriages cannot be performed by an Australian-authorised celebrant or registered in Australia, and are generally recognised if valid in the overseas country and would have been valid here. The right to marry in Australia is no longer determined by sex or gender.
facts.use_note: Covers same-sex marriages valid in Greece under the general rule (Marriage Act 1961, Part VA, cited by name only).

facts.claim: Passport name change: the Passport Office always requires an RBDM name change certificate if you were born in Australia and married overseas. You may keep using your current passport after marriage; book travel in the name in your passport.

NSW Registry: foreign documents not in English must be translated in full and stamped by a NAATI-accredited translator. The 'no registration needed' exemption for taking a spouse's name is worded for marriages in Australia.
facts.publisher: NSW Government, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages
facts.use_note: NSW only; tell readers to check their own state registry.

facts.claim: Smartraveller's Greece advice (level: exercise normal safety precautions) says Greece is in the Schengen area; Australians can enter for a short stay (90 days or less) without a visa in some cases, must register biometric details under the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) on arrival, and should check EES and visa rules before travel. ETIAS is not yet operating; the EU will announce its launch date several months ahead.
facts.use_note: Date inconsistency carried from source pack (source_date after checked; Smartraveller 'still current at' uses Australian time). Re-checked in step 3 if possible.

facts.claim: A Santorini wedding typically costs from €4,000 for an elopement to €55,000 or more, depending on guest count and style.
facts.use_note: Own page. EUR. H1 says 'From a Real Couple' but no couple is named (Nic).

facts.claim: Elopement: 2 to 20 guests, €4,000 to €12,000. Micro wedding: 20 to 40 guests, €18,000 to €30,000. Standard wedding: 50 to 80 guests, €30,000 to €55,000. Luxury wedding: 80+ guests, €55,000+.
facts.use_note: EUR. For an AUD 150K+ couple the 'Luxury 80+' band is the relevant row.

facts.claim: Venue rental runs €400 to €1,500 or more, while catering is priced at €75 to €160 or more a head. A wedding planner typically costs €3,000 to €5,000 or more, and helps with local Greek paperwork, translators and day-of coordination. Florals €1,500 to €12,000+, photography €600 to €3,000+; accommodation is a separate part of the budget.
facts.use_note: EUR.

facts.claim: On long-term averages at Heraklion and near Chania, May and September bring highs of about 24 to 27 degrees with few rain days, while most rain falls between October and April.
facts.use_note: Climate claim on our own page; no HNMS source. Crete page gives no total cost figure.

facts.claim: Greece is never just one island. It is Santorini's caldera sunsets and the whitewashed glamour of Mykonos, the wild beauty of Crete, the history of Athens, and the quiet romance of Corfu and Paros. Greece offers more than one stage for a wedding: Santorini's caldera drama, Mykonos energy, Crete's beaches and estates, the glamour of the Athens Riviera. Most couples still start with Santorini.
facts.use_note: Hub page (title 'Greece Wedding Venues: Curated Island & Mainland Luxury'). Island list as worded. Link target for the article.

facts.claim: Hub venue edit: 'Le Ciel, Imerovigli. A sought-after clifftop venue with open-air terraces for caldera ceremonies and elegant indoor space for receptions of up to around 120 guests.' 'Santorini Gem, Pyrgos. A private luxury estate with panoramic views, generous green space, and high-end dining.' 'Cavo Ventus, Akrotiri. An intimate, romantic villa built around a 200-year-old stone windmill, suited to elopements and small celebrations.' 'Rocabella, Imerovigli. Cliffside ceremonies around infinity pools, with flexible arrangements from elopements through to full receptions.'
facts.use_note: SITE-CONFLICT-G1: Le Ciel 'up to around 120 guests' here vs 'up to 80 seated guests' on the Santorini cost page (F-26 use_note). Venue sites not checked. Do not state a Le Ciel capacity until the venue confirms.

facts.claim: Mykonos: 'Cosmopolitan, glamorous, and built for couples who want a celebration with energy: beach-club receptions, whitewashed chapels, and late nights under the stars. Many couples pair the two, an intimate Santorini ceremony and a Mykonos reception, or use Mykonos as the welcome event.'
facts.use_note: Positioning, not a fact claim. Honeymoon islands on the same page: Santorini, Mykonos, Crete, Milos, Naxos and Paros.

facts.claim: Hub page: 'The season runs May through October, and the locals will tell you the sweet spots are May and early June and again in September.' 'Ceremonies are usually held in the late afternoon, around five o'clock, to catch the golden hour.'
facts.use_note: SITE-CONFLICT-G2: the best-time guide (F-33) covers April to October and names venues taking ceremonies from April and Crete 'pleasant from April to November'. Prefer the best-time guide's station data.

facts.claim: Hub legal section: 'U.S. citizens can legally marry in Greece without residing there.' Documents 'typically' include 'full birth certificates, a certificate of no impediment to marriage, passports, and any divorce or name-change certificates', 'translated by a certified translator and apostilled'. 'Many couples choose a symbolic ceremony in Santorini and handle the legal civil paperwork at home.'
facts.use_note: Do NOT cite for legal facts; use official F-01 to F-22. Written for US readers; says the advisor 'coordinates the legalities', against our rule that legal confirmation sits with the municipality and the Australian Embassy. Flag to Nic. The 'symbolic ceremony plus legal marriage at home' option is consistent with F-20 but needs an Australian-side line.

facts.claim: Best-time guide station table (HNMS long-term averages, average maximum / rain days): May Naxos 22.1°C / 3.6, Heraklion 23.6°C / 4.6, Rodos 24.1°C / 4.4, Kerkyra 24.0°C / 7.7. July Naxos 27.1°C / 0.4, Kerkyra 31.2°C. August Kerkyra 31.5°C / 3.3, Rodos 30.7°C / 0.1. September Naxos 25.1°C / 1.9, Heraklion 26.6°C / 2.8. October Naxos 21.9°C / 5.5, Heraklion 23.6°C / 7.5, Chania Souda 23.5°C / 9.3, Kerkyra 23.2°C / 11.4. April is the coolest month (Naxos 18.7°C, Heraklion 20.1°C).
facts.publisher: Wedded Wonderland (citing Hellenic National Meteorological Service station averages)
facts.use_note: Our page relays HNMS; HNMS station pages not re-read here. Naxos stands in for the Cyclades (no Santorini station in the table). Link to this page rather than repeat the table.

facts.claim: Best-time guide: 'Smartraveller warns that summer heatwaves are frequent in Greece and that wildfires occur from June to September, so high-summer weddings need shade, water and evening timing.' Smartraveller also notes ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly because of strong winds, and that Saharan dust storms are increasing, particularly in spring.
facts.use_note: Cite Smartraveller Greece directly at the claim (see step 3).

facts.claim: Best-time guide: 'The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia lists these dates when marriages are not permitted: 13 December until Christmas Day; 5 January, the eve of Epiphany; from Great Lent until Easter Sunday, with dates that vary each year; 1 to 15 August, for the Dormition of the Theotokos; 29 August; 14 September.' 'For a church wedding in Greece, ask your priest and the local Metropolis.'
facts.publisher: Wedded Wonderland (relaying the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia)
facts.use_note: Archdiocese page not re-read here; these are Australian Archdiocese dates, not Church of Greece. Keep the 'ask your priest and Metropolis' line.

facts.claim: Packages guide: 'Greece wedding packages usually bundle the ceremony, its set-up, a coordinator and some help with the paperwork. Guest rooms, exclusive use, transfers and outside suppliers are where they part ways.' 'On Santorini, the venues in this guide quote weddings rather than publish set tiers.' 'Grace Hotel requires a wedding planner for every wedding.'
facts.use_note: Venue-level details relayed from venue sites, not re-checked here. Link rather than repeat the ten-question checklist.

facts.claim: Packages guide, Orthodox conditions at one venue group: 'At the Elounda Collection, one partner must be Christian Orthodox, both must be baptised Orthodox, Roman Catholic or Protestant, and the wedding needs Metropolis approval.' The Elounda Collection 'states that these [symbolic] ceremonies are not legally recognised in Greece'. Its checklist: every document apostilled, translated into Greek and issued within three months of the wedding; the couple registers the marriage in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days.
facts.use_note: Venue terms, not official. SITE-CONFLICT-G3: 'issued within three months of the wedding' (venue) vs Athens 'issued within the last six months' of lodging (F-10). 40-day registration is still unconfirmed on any official page (carried gap). Attribute to the venue if used.

facts.claim: Same-sex guide: 'Since 16 February 2024, Greek law has allowed civil marriage between two people of the same sex.' Law 5089/2024 'was voted on 15 February 2024 and published in the Government Gazette on 16 February 2024'. 'The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia describes its sacrament of marriage as the union of a man and a woman.'
facts.use_note: Consistent with official F-13 (law number and civil scope). Dates from our page only; cite F-13 for the law and link this page for detail.

facts.claim: Same-sex guide, relaying Smartraveller: 'Same-sex relationships are legal, though attitudes vary throughout the country. Avoid public displays of affection, especially in rural areas. Attitudes are generally more accepting on Greek islands such as Mykonos, Santorini and Ios.' Also: the Australian Embassy in Athens says apostilled documents and CNIs are ready for collection within two working days, by appointment Monday to Friday 9:00am to 12:30pm, and the embassy does not give legal advice.
facts.publisher: Wedded Wonderland (relaying Smartraveller and the Australian Embassy Athens)
facts.use_note: Re-check both claims on the official pages before citing (step 3). The 'two working days' line is newer than the embassy page read on 12 Nov (F-14) and conflicts with DFAT's 'processing times vary' only in scope (Athens counter vs DFAT in Australia).

facts.claim: Same-sex guide: 'Australians can visit for short stays without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.' Rhodes asks for 'a marriage licence or certificate of no impediment to marriage for each of you ... naming the person you will marry and valid for six months'; translations 'by a Greek lawyer, the Greek Embassy abroad or the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs'.
facts.publisher: Wedded Wonderland (relaying the Municipality of Rhodes)
facts.use_note: SITE-CONFLICT-G4: '90 days in any 180-day period' here vs '90 days or less ... in some cases' on the licence page and Smartraveller (F-23). Rhodes translation list predates the 2021 MFA reform (F-11). Rhodes municipal page not read here.

facts.claim: Licence guide: 'Gov.gr lists eight days for the Greek marriage licence: a seven-day wait for objections, then one day to grant it.' 'Couples living abroad may not need a Greek licence at all if their home-country certificate names their partner, so confirm with DFAT and your town hall whether your Australian CNI does.' 'We could not find an official page for Santorini (Thira) or Mykonos.' 'If the paperwork does not suit your timeline, marry legally in Australia and hold a symbolic ceremony in Greece; an Australian celebrant cannot legally marry you overseas.'
facts.use_note: Our page; built from the official facts reused here (F-01 to F-22). Graded consistent. Link as the legal spoke. Note it also says 'Your Wedded Concierge can handle the town-hall emails, translations and timeline', which is help, not legal confirmation.

facts.claim: Venues guide (title 'Greece Wedding Venues: 20 From the Islands to Athens'): '20 venues across seven regions.' 'Guest count decides the region: Santorini's caldera terraces seat 15 to 60, while venues on the Athens Riviera and in Crete publish space for several hundred. Exclusive use can mean a chosen event space or the whole hotel, and only a few venues, such as Canaves, Katikies and Melenos, offer the whole hotel.' 'Lagonissi is about 20 minutes from the airport, and Amanzoe is 2.5 hours.'
facts.use_note: SITE-CONFLICT-G5: 'Santorini's caldera terraces seat 15 to 60' vs hub 'Le Ciel ... receptions of up to around 120 guests' (F-29) and the same venues page listing Canaves Oia Suites 'up to 120'. Likely terraces vs whole-property reception, but pages do not reconcile it. For an AUD 150K+ couple with 80 to 120 guests this matters: do not state a Santorini ceiling without the venue's own figure.

facts.claim: Venues guide: 'Greece has a Mediterranean climate with plenty of sunshine and little rain, and in summer the dry, hot days are cooled by seasonal winds called the meltemi. The wind that cools a terrace can also hold up a ferry, so plan both.'
facts.use_note: Consistent with F-33/F-34 (north wind, ferry delays). Climate description is ours; HNMS not re-read.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Greece: 'Overall: Exercise normal safety precautions' (advice level green). Still current at 25 November 2026; updated 30 September 2026.
facts.use_note: Supersedes the level line in F-23. 'Still current at' is Smartraveller's own date (Australian time).

facts.claim: Smartraveller Greece: 'Australians can travel to the Schengen area for short trips without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.' On arrival for a short stay (90 days or less) on an Australian passport you have fingerprints and a photo taken under the EES; 'The EES is free. You don't need to do anything before arriving at the border.' 'There is no confirmed date for the implementation of ETIAS. The European Union will announce the date several months before its launch.'
facts.use_note: RESOLVES SITE-CONFLICT-G4: '90 days in any 180-day period' is Smartraveller's wording; the licence page's '90 days or less ... in some cases' is also on the page (summary). Use the 90-in-180 line. Replaces F-23 for entry facts.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Greece: 'Wildfires occur during the extended summer period, from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations.' 'Heatwaves are frequent over the summer months. They can cause heat exhaustion, heat stroke and death.' 'Storms of dust from the Sahara Desert are increasing in frequency across Greece, particularly during Spring.'
facts.use_note: Official source for the season section; matches our best-time page (F-34).

facts.claim: Smartraveller Greece: 'Greece is in an active seismic zone and experiences earthquakes and volcanic activity, including near major tourist destinations such as the islands of Santorini and Crete.' 'Frequent and sustained seismic activity occurred near the Cycladic islands in early 2025.'
facts.use_note: Relevant to Santorini planning and insurance; one calm line only.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Greece, sea travel: 'Ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly due to strong winds.' 'During the tourist season, from May to October, be prepared for high temperatures and large crowds at popular seaports.' 'Some services don't provide suitable access for people with disabilities.' 'In most cases, you'll need to carry your luggage up and down stairs.'
facts.use_note: Guest logistics and accessibility for older guests (paying_parent persona).

facts.claim: Smartraveller Greece: 'There's no agreement between Australia and Greece for free healthcare. Tourists must pay for all medical care, even if they need to stay in hospital or be evacuated.' 'If you become seriously ill or injured, you may need evacuation. This is more likely if you're in a remote area or on a Greek island.' Travel insurance 'must cover all medical costs overseas, including evacuation.'
facts.use_note: Guest insurance line.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Greece: 'Same-sex relationships are legal, though attitudes vary throughout the country. Avoid public displays of affection, especially in rural areas. Attitudes are generally more accepting on Greek islands such as Mykonos, Santorini and Ios.' 'Racially motivated and homophobic attacks have occurred.' The official currency is the Euro; amounts over 10,000 euros must be declared when travelling between Greece and a non-EU country.
facts.use_note: Confirms our same-sex page quote (F-39). The Local customs section also says 'Same-sex relationships are legal but isn't widely accepted'; quote the main line. Male Australian-Greek dual nationals may have military service obligations; get advice from a Greek embassy or consulate before travel (useful for Greek-Australian couples).

facts.claim: Santorini cost page (re-read today, headline figures unchanged): 'Guest lists at many caldera venues are capped at about 30, which is why larger celebrations usually move to a different property and a higher tier.' 'Le Ciel ... with a stated capacity of up to 80 seated guests for its ceremony and reception format.' 'Four-course set menus typically run €76 to €110 a head, and an open bar or hourly drinks package adds €20 to €45 per person an hour.' 'Many international couples choose to complete their legal marriage at home and hold a symbolic ceremony in Santorini.'
facts.use_note: SITE-CONFLICT-G5 extended, four figures for Santorini capacity across our pages: 'capped at about 30' (this page), '15 to 60' (venues guide, F-42), Le Ciel '80 seated' (this page) vs 'around 120' (hub, F-29). Do not publish a capacity until Nic or the venue settles it. H1 still says 'From a Real Couple' with no couple named (carried N-06). F-24 to F-26 reconfirmed. EUR.

facts.claim: Australian Embassy Athens marriage page, re-read today, is unchanged: 'Each year many Australians choose to marry in Greece, particularly on the islands.' A CNI 'is required by both religious and municipal organisations for each non-Greek citizen'; acceptable place of issue 'can differ significantly between organisations'; first contact 'the priest or celebrant who is to marry you, or your wedding planner'. It still names the MFA Translation Section.
facts.use_note: Confirms F-14 and F-15 today. Translation line remains superseded by F-11. The page does not carry the 'two working days' or appointment-hours claim relayed on our same-sex page (F-39); that may sit on the embassy's notarial page (not read). Do not use the two-day figure without it.

legal.summary: Civil and Orthodox weddings both need the mayor's licence (or for non-residents its foreign equivalent). Confirm with the municipality where you marry.
Residents' licence: one-week objection wait, 8 days end to end on gov.gr, valid 6 months.
2019 Interior circular: a foreign no-impediment document naming the spouse stands in for the Greek licence. Confirm with the town hall and the Australian Embassy Athens.
Chania non-resident list: home licence naming the partner, apostille, originals.
Heraklion non-resident list and one adult witness each.
Official Greek translations via the MFA Register of Certified Translators since 1 Sep 2021.
Law 5089/2024: civil marriage for same-sex couples.
Australian Embassy Athens: CNI required for each non-Greek party; place of issue varies by organisation.
DFAT issues CNIs; at least one applicant must be an Australian citizen or PR.
No Australian registration; overseas marriage generally recognised if valid in Greece and would be valid in Australia.
Australian-born spouse married overseas needs an RBDM change of name certificate for a passport in the married name.
Australians: up to 90 days in any 180-day period visa-free; EES on arrival; ETIAS not yet operating.

site_conflicts.detail: Four different figures: hub Le Ciel 'up to around 120' (F-29); Santorini cost page Le Ciel 'up to 80 seated' and 'many caldera venues are capped at about 30' (F-51); venues guide 'caldera terraces seat 15 to 60' and Canaves Oia Suites 'up to 120' (F-42). Nic to settle; check venue sites.

Hub: 'season runs May through October' (F-31). Best-time guide covers April to October with venues taking ceremonies from April (F-33). Smartraveller says the tourist season at seaports is May to October (F-48). Prefer the best-time guide plus Smartraveller.

Packages guide relays Elounda Collection 'issued within three months of the wedding' (F-37); Athens says 'within the last six months' of lodging (F-10). Venue-specific vs municipal; say 'ask your town hall'.
Resolved: Smartraveller says 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period' (F-45). The licence page's '90 days or less ... in some cases' is incomplete, not wrong.

Hub is written for U.S. citizens and says the advisor 'coordinates the legalities' (F-32), against house rule that legal confirmation sits with the municipality and Australian Embassy. The licence page (F-41) is the correct legal spoke.

needs.what: Whether the DFAT CNI names the intended spouse (decides whether non-resident Australians skip the Greek licence per F-05).
needs.who: Wedded Advisor to check with DFAT and a recent client CNI; legal confirmation from the town hall and the Australian Embassy Athens

needs.what: Current Thira (Santorini) and Mykonos town hall practice for non-resident Australians: documents, newspaper notice, wait, ceremony days, outdoor settings. No official page found.
needs.who: Wedded Advisor to gather; confirmation from the municipality itself

needs.what: Settle Santorini capacity wording across our pages (SITE-CONFLICT-G1/G5) and confirm Le Ciel's capacity with the venue.
A real Greek wedding for an AUD 150K+ couple (guest count, island, total in AUD) with consent; the Santorini cost page H1 says 'From a Real Couple' but names none.

An AUD budget figure for a luxury Greece wedding from our own pages or quotes. All our Greece figures are EUR; the top published band is 'Luxury wedding: 80+ guests, €55,000+'. No own figure covers Mykonos, Crete totals, Athens Riviera or mainland estates.
Greek Orthodox conditions from an official Church of Greece or Metropolis source (baptism, sponsor, mixed marriages, fees). Only a venue's terms are on our site (F-37).
Registration deadline (40 days) and apostille on the Greek marriage certificate: no official page read confirms either authority or deadline.
